summary: Terra Mystica is a no-luck strategy game where each player's asymmetric faction terraforms hex terrain to expand a network of buildings, upgrade structures, and climb four cult tracks. Games are quiet and cerebral, with success coming from efficient long-term resource planning rather than direct confrontation.
praised: deep, satisfying economic engine with zero luck
highly asymmetric factions that each play differently
rewarding for players who like optimization puzzles
criticised: steep learning curve and a slow, unrewarding first play
can feel dry and math-heavy rather than thematic
needs a full table and careful faction balance to sing

interaction.detail: All players terraform and build on one shared hex map, so adjacent territory and terrain conversion are directly contested, and reaching a spot first (or a favorable cult-track slot) denies it to everyone else. There is no combat or card market; conflict is purely positional and about turn-order priority on shared tracks.

sources: Round scoring bonuses for building actions/cult advances
Largest connected network of structures (final scoring)
scoring.how_you_win: Over exactly six rounds you earn VP by building and upgrading structures, advancing on cult tracks, and forming towns, with the largest connected area and top cult positions scored at the end; most total VP wins.
scoring.score_note: higher in 2p, lower with more players
